title: P0 hostedapi connection fencepost surge postmortem
body:
Summary:

On 2029-11-26 02:13 UTC Redwood hosted API experienced a P0 outage affecting streaming and short-lived request paths for ~35 minutes. Symptoms were a rapid rise in 5xx rates and p95/p99 TTFB for streaming sessions across multiple regions, followed by connection churn and eviction cascades on edge proxies. Total customer-visible error rate peaked at ~7.2% for streaming calls and ~2.3% for non-streaming text-generation; most impact was concentrated on enterprise customers with long-lived sockets and high multiplexing.

Impact:
- Duration: ~02:13 UTC -> ~02:48 UTC (35 minutes) with residual noise until 03:10 UTC.
- Scope: Global but highest error surface in us-west1 and eu-west1.
- Customer impact: Streaming responses truncated, reconnect storms observed, degraded latency for short text-generation requests. Several enterprise customers reported disruption to production features (support tickets INC-2029-2213, INC-2029-2214).
- Severity: P0 (SRE and Eng escalation).

Detection and Alerting:
- First alert triggered by streaming 5xx SLO alarm at 02:15 UTC (oncall SRE paging).
- Secondary signals: jump in outbound connection churn metric (edge-proxy.conn_reconnect_rate), increase in kernel TIME_WAIT sockets on a subset of proxies, and rapid growth in acceptor backlog on multiplexing tier.
- Pager/Slack: SRE runbook channel used; product ops alerted. Detection worked but initial triage underestimated coupling to KV-prefetch throttles.

Timeline (high level):
- 02:13 UTC: small spike in p99 streaming latency recorded, automated alerting threshold crossed at 02:15 UTC.
- 02:16–02:22 UTC: oncall assesses; observes correlated rise in reconnects and 5xx; rollouts team confirms no recent deploys.
- 02:23 UTC: mitigation attempts - increase edge proxy acceptor thread pool size (temporary) and enable aggressive keepalive backoff on a subset of front-line proxies.
- 02:27 UTC: temporary mitigation reduces p99 in one region but another region shows delayed recovery; KV-prefetch queue saturation observed on dedicated backend nodes.
- 02:31 UTC: engineers identify recurring pattern where many clients reconnect simultaneously after a ~30s keepalive jitter (fencepost alignment).
- 02:36 UTC: implemented patch to stagger reconnect responses at edge (randomized 0–250ms) and throttle prefetch concurrency per-tenant.
- 02:44 UTC: global error rate begins to return to baseline; by 02:48 UTC primary symptoms resolved.
- 03:10 UTC: residual telemetry noise subsided; full verification completed.

Root Cause:
Primary root cause: a timing alignment of client reconnects (keepalive rotation) created a "fencepost" surge in simultaneous new session handshakes that amplified KV-prefetch load and caused acceptor backlogs on multiplexing front-ends. This in turn caused queueing and timeouts in the streaming path, leading to increased 5xx and connection churn.

Contributing factors:
- Keepalive jitter reduction in a recent client SDK release (sdk-js v3.8.1) tightened client timers to 30s with low jitter; many large customers upgraded in the same maintenance window, increasing synchronized reconnect probability.
- KV-prefetch worker pool sizing is optimized for steady-state but had limited burst headroom; prefetch tasks blocked on a shared L1 metadata lock under bursts.
- Edge-proxy acceptor thread pool and multiplex queue depths were tuned aggressively to reduce latency, leaving little headroom for sudden spike in connection setup work.
- Telemetry gaps: acceptor backlog alarm had an alert threshold but no automatic mitigator (we had detection but no automated graduated throttling).

Why previous mitigations didn't stop this:
- Autoscaler for backend prefetch capacity reacts in minutes and did not scale fast enough for a sharp sub-minute surge.
- Early mitigation heuristics focused on per-connection rate limiting, which failed to address the metadata lock contention in KV-prefetch.

Immediate mitigations taken:
- Staggered reconnects at edge: introduced small randomized delay (0–250ms) when detecting reconstructed client sessions from the same IP/tenant block.
- Throttled per-tenant prefetch concurrency on the busiest backend nodes to prevent lock saturation.
- Increased acceptor thread pool on a targeted set of edge proxies to relieve temporary backlog.
- Manual traffic steering: shifted a subset of noisy tenant traffic off hotspots to healthy rings.
- Applied a short-term rate cap for anonymous streaming sessions for 20 minutes to reduce noise; explicit enterprise tenants exempted after manual review.

Effectiveness of mitigations:
- Staggered reconnects reduced measured synchronous connection events by ~78% in impacted nodes.
- Prefetch concurrency throttle lowered median prefetch latency from ~220ms to ~70ms under load.
- Acceptors increase reduced acceptor backlog indicators but was an operationally heavy-handed fix.

Long-term remediation and action items (owners and ETA):
1) SDK guidance and opt-out: Work with SDK teams to publish updated guidance and release a minor SDK patch that adds jitter to keepalive timers; coordinate with client success to notify large customers. Owner: product-dx (Maya Li). ETA: 2029-12-10.
2) Prefetch redesign: Remove the single L1 metadata lock by sharding prefetch work by tenant and key-hash; increase worker headroom and introduce bounded queueing with graceful degradation. Owner: eng-serving-runtime (Jamal Nguyen). ETA: 2029-02-28 (design), 2029-05-15 (rollout).
3) Rapid autoscaling for short bursts: Implement a fast-path scale-up for prefetch/backends with sub-minute scale policy and warm standby capacity. Owner: infra-autoscaler (Kenji Sato). ETA: 2029-01-30.
4) Edge reconnect smoothing: Permanent implementation of reconnect staggering with configurable jitter and an opt-out list for latency-sensitive enterprise tenants. Owner: eng-edge (Sofia Romero). ETA: 2029-12-05.
5) Runbook automation: Add automated graduated throttling actions when acceptor backlog > threshold for 30s (throttle new sessions, enable reconnect jitter, surface mitigation runbook). Owner: eng-sre (Aisha Patel). ETA: 2029-12-01.
6) Telemetry: Add new metric and dashboard for prefetch lock contention rate and per-tenant connection fanout hotspots; create Playbook runbook links directly on alarm. Owner: observability (Ravi Shah). ETA: 2029-12-01.
7) Chaos test: Add a scheduled chaos experiment that simulates synchronized reconnect storms at scale to validate mitigations. Owner: sres-chaos (Alexei Morozov). ETA: 2029-12-20.

Runbook updates (immediate changes made):
- New checklist step when streaming 5xx/tcp churn occurs: check edge.conn_reconnect_rate + prefetch.queue_wait_ms together.
- Add prescriptive mitigation sequence: 1) apply reconnect jitter at edge, 2) throttle per-tenant prefetch concurrency, 3) increase acceptor threads for affected rings, 4) route noisy tenants.
- Added script snippets for safe acceptor thread pool expansion and a one-click traffic-shift play for rings.

On-call notes and lessons learned:
- Communications: earlier communication to customers (esp large tenants) about coordinated client SDK upgrades could have reduced synchronized behavior. Work with CSM to create a notification protocol for timed SDK pushes.
- Avoid manual acceptor scaling as a first-line fix; prefer targeted behavioral mitigations (staggering, throttles) because acceptor changes have downstream JVM/native memory side-effects.
- We need a canary for client-sdk behavioral changes: a short-window dark-release to a subset of customers to detect mass timer alignment.
- Incident commander: Aisha Patel; Eng lead: Jamal Nguyen; Edge lead: Sofia Romero; Infra lead: Kenji Sato. Communication channel: #sre-incident-2213.

Follow-ups and verification plan:
- Verification plan for each action item above included in linked linear tickets. Post-deploy canary window: 72 hours of elevated telemetry watch for reconverging traffic patterns.
- Acceptance criteria for prefetch redesign: per-tenant 95th prefetch latency under stress + no single lock saturation event in 1M simulated sessions.

Appendix: Relevant signals and queries:
- edge.conn_reconnect_rate by ring, tenant (timeseries).
- prefetch.queue_wait_ms 95/99 percentile.
- acceptor.backlog_count and acceptor.thread_utilization by proxy.
- netstat TIME_WAIT spikes across proxies.
- SDK rollout window: client-sdk release list for 2029-11-25 to 2029-11-27.

Notes to self / raw fragments (working):
- Consider per-tenant circuit-breaker for new session establishment if reconnect rate exceeds configured window.
- Evaluate adding ephemeral prefetch tokens that expire to control burst concurrency.
- Need a short RFC for backpressure propagation from prefetch layer -> client-facing edge (so we avoid head-of-line effects).

Status: Draft postmortem. Action items created in Linear and assigned. Will follow up with a cross-team retro session next week to finalize timelines and close action items.

Owner for postmortem: Aisha Patel (eng-sre).
